agree.reason: The declining-ad framing, the pace comparison and the six-month checkpoint will win most of the board, but the two ad-background members will notice that it never explains why ads can't run alongside membership or how the first-year cash gap is covered while membership ramps up from about $20,000.

honest.reason: It turns the brief's 'will replace within a year' into a target with a review, leaves a placeholder for pilot retention instead of making up a figure, and calls the pilot sign-ups likely loyal early adopters; its only addition is an unquantified allowance for fees and cancellations.

works_the_facts.reason: Every derived figure checks out and is useful: 36% decline, about $65–70k projected, 1.5% conversion, about $20k a year from the pilot, 875 members to break even, 7% of the list, and 15 a week needed against about 35 a week already reached.

right_comparison.reason: It correctly treats the alternative as a declining source rather than a flat $84,000 and projects the trend forward, though it doesn't compare against a hybrid that keeps ads during the transition.

qualification.reason: The hedge can be checked: monthly reporting, a 500-member midpoint at six months, and named fallback options (pricing, marketing, limited sponsorships), though 'well short' and 'bring options' leave what happens on a miss a little soft.

objections.reason: It answers the early-adopter concern and treats the long-serving salesperson with respect, but it misses the ad members' most obvious objections: why not keep ads as well, and how to cover the revenue drop in the first months.

fit.reason: It's a clean board memo that leads with the decision and runs to roughly one page, perhaps slightly over once the placeholders are filled in.
